textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 social-science · The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A civilisation is a stage of human society with cities, specialised work, trade, planning, shared rules and a way of keeping records.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A civilisation is a stage of human society with cities, specialised work, trade, planning, shared rules and a way of keeping records. Civilisation began at different times in different parts of the world.
beats.speakEn: A civilisation is a stage of human society with cities, specialised work, trade, planning, shared rules and a way of keeping records. Civilisation began at different times in different parts of the world.

beats.en: It grew in the northwest of the Subcontinent around the Indus river and the now dried Sarasvati river, in parts of present-day India and Pakistan, with mountain ranges forming natural boundaries.

textbookBox.concept: Cities were carefully planned. Streets ran at right angles and houses were built of baked or sun-dried bricks of standard sizes.

beats.en: Cities were carefully planned. Streets ran at right angles and houses were built of baked or sun-dried bricks of standard sizes.
beats.speakEn: Cities were carefully planned. Streets ran at right angles and houses were built of baked or sun-dried bricks of standard sizes.

beats.en: People farmed wheat, barley, peas and cotton, kept cattle and made pottery, copper and bronze tools and beautiful beads and ornaments. Stone weights of fixed sizes and measuring rods were used for fair trade.
